hero.caption: Segmented panorama of the east side of the Old Stone House. The large first floor kitchen in the rear of the home can be reached through the door seen here on the east side. The Colonial Revival garden is accessed by the small flight of stone steps seen at the far right. M St NW is visible at the far left. The original images were taken on April 6, 2011. This is a retouched image; a section of sky along the top of the image was recreated to correct stitching/cropping errors.

images.caption: The Old Stone House located at 3051 M Street, NW in the Georgetown neighborhood of Washington, D.C. Built in 1765, the Old Stone House is the city's oldest building on its original foundation. It's listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is a contributing property to the Georgetown Historic District. The back yard has been turned into an English garden and the home now operates as a museum.

images.caption: This is the basin at the end of the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal, looking north toward the end of the canal. Guard lock #8 is at the end of the channel on the left. Interstate Highway 68 / US 40 / US 220 runs on that bridge in the background. The Cumberland Masonic Temple and the Emmanuel Episcopal Church are visible to the left, beyond the highway bridge. The Western Maryland Station is just visiable (brick building, center of picture) beyond the highway bridge. Shops at Canal Place are to the right of the basin. Potomac River is to the left, just beyond the flood wall.
